# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 95 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 50 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_095_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 95

**1** Jesus said: "If you have money, do not lend it at interest.

**2** Rather, give it to one from whom you will not get it back."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**"Lend at interest"** — *toubo*: the Coptic word specifically denotes usurious lending.

**"Rather"** — EMET preferred over "Instead" (LOGOS): the Coptic adversative particle suggests the stronger redirecting contrast.

**Theological Note:** Thomas goes beyond the Q prohibition on usury (Luke 6:34-35) to a more radical instruction: do not lend at all — give to those who cannot repay. The criterion for legitimate generosity is precisely the impossibility of repayment. This mirrors the beatitude logic: give without calculation.

**Synoptic Parallels:** Luke 6:34-35 ("lend, expecting nothing in return"). Thomas intensifies this: not lending-without-interest but giving-without-return.
